why: `DomainIdParse` / `DomainIdRange` -- and the point is that they are ERRORS. Issue 0206: a malformed or out-of-range domain id used to be a silent fallback to domain 0 in C++ and a silent no-op in this resolver. On a desktop that is a nuisance you notice in `ros2 node list`; on a board it is the whole failure, because a device that came up on the wrong domain looks exactly like a device with a dead radio -- it has no console anyone reads, no way to be asked what domain it chose, and often no way to be interrupted. So a typo in `ROS_DOMAIN_ID` refuses to boot rather than joining a graph nobody is watching. rclrs surfaces the equivalent as an `RclrsError` carrying a string, which `rust:RclrsError` in the types stage already records as unavailable under no_std. The ladder these errors guard is `c:get_default_domain_id`. phase-484 W8c added `RetiredEnvVar { name, replacement }`: a set `ZENOH_LOCATOR` / `ZENOH_MODE` (retired aliases, `rust:RETIRED_ENV_VARS`) refuses to boot for the same reason — ignoring it would dial the default router.
